Having the fishmonger remove the bones m: Sea bass in parchment (papillote)
Cut the vegetables into julienne and place on baking paper.
Put the fish on top and add oil, lemon, dill and salt.
Close the paper into a parcel.
The steam inside the parcel keeps the fish moist.
Serve by opening the parcel at the table.
Shrimp and vegetable rice
300 g shrimp
1 dessert spoon salt, turmeric
Stir the shrimp in butter for 2 minutes and remove.
Fry the pepper and rice.
Add the water, salt, turmeric and peas.
Add the shrimp and let rest for 10 minutes.
Warming the shrimp during resting is enough.
Salmon and spinach pasta
200 g salmon
Dice the salmon and cook in oil for 4 minutes.
Add the garlic and spinach and let wilt.
Add the cream.
Smoked salmon can also be used.
Grilled trout (with almonds)
2 trout
3 tablespoons flaked almonds
Salt the fish and grill for 5 minutes on each side.
Toast the almonds in butter for 2 minutes.
Add the lemon juice.
Drizzle over the fish.
Take care not to burn the almonds.
Grilled sea bream
2 sea bream
1 bunch rocket, 1 red onion
Score the fish diagonally.
Rub with oil and salt.
Grill on a very hot grill for 6–7 minutes on each side.
Squeeze over lemon.
Serve with rocket and onion.
If the grill isn’t hot enough, the fish sticks.
Beetroot hummus
1 teaspoon cumin, salt
Chop the beetroot.
Put all the ingredients in a food processor.
Blend until smooth; add iced water if needed.
Spread on a plate.
Beetroot gives hummus a vivid colour and sweetness.
Samphire salad
300 g samphire
Wash the samphire and blanch in boiling water for 4 minutes.
Transfer to cold water.
Strip off the fibrous parts.
Mix with garlic, oil and lemon.
Samphire is salty; don’t add salt.
Cold, with fish.
Muhammara
1 dessert spoon cumin, chilli flakes
Peel the peppers.
Pulse all the ingredients briefly in a food processor.
Adjust the consistency with breadcrumbs.
Don’t over-blend so it keeps some texture.
Stuffed zucchini flowers
16 zucchini flowers
Half a bunch dill and mint
1 teaspoon salt, sugar
Carefully remove the pistils from inside the flowers.
Fry the onion in oil and make a filling with the rice, herbs and spices.
Fill the flowers halfway and twist the tips closed.
Arrange in a pot and add 1 glass of hot water and oil.
Cook over low heat for 30 minutes and let cool.
Don’t fill completely, as the rice will swell.
Atom (yogurt with fried dried chillies)
4 dried hot chillies
Whisk the yogurt with garlic and spread on a plate.
Fry the dried chillies in oil for 1 minute.
Place the chillies on the yogurt.
Drizzle with the oil.
If the chillies are very hot, use fewer.
Stuffed vine leaves in olive oil
500 g vine leaves
3 onions
Half a cup olive oil
2 tablespoons currants and pine nuts
1 dessert spoon mint, allspice, cinnamon, salt, sugar
Fry the onions in oil, add the pine nuts, rice and spices; cook with half a glass of water for 5 minutes.
Blanch the leaves and cut off the stems.
Put filling on the leaves and roll up tightly.
Arrange in a pot, add lemon and 2 glasses of hot water and weigh down with a plate.
Cook over low heat for 45 minutes and let cool in the pot.
Rolling tightly prevents them unrolling during cooking.
Cold, with lemon.
Stuffed peppers in olive oil
10 peppers for stuffing
1 dessert spoon mint, salt, sugar
Fry the onion in oil and add the rice, tomato and spices.
Cook with half a glass of water for 5 minutes.
Stuff the peppers and put their caps back on.
Arrange in a pot and add 1.5 glasses of hot water.
Cook for 40 minutes and let cool.
The filling should be half-cooked; it finishes in the pot.
Baba ghanoush (smoky eggplant)
Char the eggplants and peel.
Finely dice the tomato and pepper.
Chop the eggplant with a knife.
Mix everything with garlic, pomegranate molasses and oil.
Antakya-style, it’s made without tahini.
Celeriac and walnut salad (with yogurt)
2 tablespoons mayonnaise
Grate the celeriac and toss with lemon.
Mix the yogurt, mayonnaise and garlic.
Add the celeriac.
Rest for 1 hour.
After resting, the celeriac softens.
Bean pilaki (in olive oil)
Fry the onion and garlic in oil.
Add the beans and 1 glass of water.
Serve cold with lemon and parsley.
Pilaki gets tastier as it rests.
Cretan spread (Girit ezmesi)
Half a bunch dill, 4–5 sprigs mint, half a bunch parsley
Mash the white cheese and lor cheese.
Add the chopped greens.
